text:
jia: Billing alert at 03:12 UTC — sudden GPU spend spike in us-west1, ~3x baseline. Dashboard: https://billing.redwood.internal/spend/2026-03-03

sre-bot: triggered alert for cost-anomaly (threshold=200%)

matt: looking. pg: autoscaler logs + cloud events incoming. any recent infra churn?

jia: pushed a tiny Terraform rename yesterday to standardize nodepool labels (accel -> accelerator_family). I think the new label didn't land on the instance template for the 'ml-preempt' pool.

nina: if selector uses the old label name, autoscaler might not match the intended pool and fall back to the 'default-gpu' pool (which uses larger on-demand flavors).

matt: confirming with `gcloud compute instances list --filter="zone:us-west1*" --format="table(name,machineType,labels)" | grep gpu` — seeing lots of n2d-highmem-48-gpu rather than our usual a100-80gb-preempt.

jia: yep that's the anomaly. Terraform plan changed variable name but the instance-template resource still had the old label key. I must've missed the other module.

ops-oncall: scale commands? we should prevent more launches. I can set autoscaler min=0 on the fallback pool or add a quota guard.

matt: do that. patching autoscaler to block new replicas for fallback pool now: `gcloud compute instance-templates update ...` (will post exact command).

nina: also add a quick ephemeral policy: tag the default-gpu pool as `cost-lock=true` and set autoscaler max=0 until we fix infra.

sre-bot: action logged: set-pool-max default-gpu -> 0 by ops-oncall at 03:27 UTC

jia: created PR #8422 with the fix: normalize label key across modules and add a lint check that plans with label mismatches fail CI.

matt: rollback plan: 1) scale down fallback pool, 2) drain and reprovision legitimate pools with correct labels, 3) run a dry-run terraform apply in staging, 4) merge PR. Ops, help with step 1 now?

ops-oncall: done step 1. scaled fallback pool down, draining 42 nodes. watch for stuck drains (eviction timeouts).

jia: attaching relevant logs snippet:
```
autoscaler: scaleUp: launchedInstanceGroupManager=rg-default-gpu, reason=unmatchedSelector, count=38
instance-template.labels: { "accelerator_family": "", "accelerator": "v100" }
expected labels: { "accelerator_family": "a100" }
```

matt: great capture. I'll run a cost-scan to estimate total overspend and open a billing ticket for credits if eligible.

nina: follow-ups: 1) add a pre-deploy hook to validate label keys; 2) add a runtime guard that prevents autoscaler fallback to default pools without explicit allow; 3) run a 7-day retrospective on TF drift alerts.

jia: will add the pre-deploy hook in the PR and coordinate with infra-qa to run a smoke apply.

matt: closing loop — will update the incident channel with spend estimate and next steps once the drains finish. huge thanks for the quick ops response :thumbsup:

ops-oncall: monitoring drains + will re-enable fallback pool only after signoff.

jia: postmortem TODO assigned to me. short-term: revert label rename if CI misses it again. long-term: enforce label schema via policy.

matt: ack. keep this thread updated.
